text:
ajay: Heads-up: saw a p99 latency spike on the v3.6 canary around 17:04 UTC after the tokenizer changes went live. ~3x p99 for text-gen. rolling investigation.

maria: noticing kernel-decider flip to cpu-fallback on many hosts right when seqlen distribution jumps. correlated with canary traffic.

sara: can you paste the profiler output? I want to see where time went.

ajay: from one host, trimmed:```
[17:03:58] kernel-decider: selected path=cpu_fallback (score 0.72)
[17:03:58] batcher: headroom=0.12, batch_size=8
[17:03:59] kv-cache: insert_rate=420/s, evict_rate=390/s, hit_ratio=0.58
[17:03:59] inference: p50=45ms p95=320ms p99=680ms
```

dan: kv-cache churn that high with hit_ratio ~0.58 + smaller headroom explains thrashing. tokenizer change must be producing lots of long sequences and rare prefixes so KV entries don't stabilize.

leo: also saw noisy-neighbor CPU steal on host g5-12-14 at same window (sysload spiked). that likely nudged kernel-decider to safer but slower path.

maria: hypothesis: tokenizer v2 token boundaries increased avg tokens per request by ~1.9x for this workload, causing seqburst that trips the kernel-decider's seqlen_threshold heuristic. combined with eviction this pushes p99.

ajay: reproducing locally with a replay of canary traffic shows same kernel flip when seqlen distribution tail >1024.

sara: dump from kernel-decider config on affected hosts:```
kernel-decider.version=v2.4
seqlen_threshold=1024
latency_margin=0.2
prefetch_enabled=true
prefetch_batch=16
```

maria: profiling flamegraph (attached) points to large time in attention kernel switch + memory copy when falling back.

leo: short-term mitigation: pause the canary and rollback tokenizer change. also increase batcher headroom and set kernel-decider seqlen_threshold=2048 for the canary autoscale group to avoid flip.

dan: can we do a faster mitigation: force kernel path to gpu-optimized for canary hosts? riskier but quick.

ajay: I pushed a canary pause and started rollback at 17:10 UTC. runtime-bot: deployment canary paused (deployment_id=dep_9876).

runtime-bot: alert suppressed for this canary group, will resume when rollback complete.

maria: for longer fix: two tracks - 1) adjust tokenization to avoid seqburst (soft max split/recombine), 2) make kernel-decider aware of kv-cache churn: if evict_rate/birth_rate high then prefer gpu path even if seqlen crosses threshold.

sara: also add quick prewarm for kv-cache on rollout: seed common prefixes from eval set during canary start. cheap and likely to lift hit_ratio.

leo: I've annotated hosts in infra dashboard and raised a noisy-neighbor ticket to infra team to investigate CPU steal patterns.

ajay: postmortem action items: pause+rollback (done), tweak kernel-decider heuristics (maria/sara), kv prewarm for canary (sara), tokenizer patch to reduce tail (maria), add dashboard for kv churn metric (leo). scheduling a short bug scrub at 13:00 PT.

maria: quick note: if we bump seqlen_threshold we may hide real regressions for workloads that truly need gpu fallback; prefer targeted override per-deploy for now.

dan: I’ll run a simulation with synthetic tail-heavy traffic to validate the kernel-decider change before we flip in prod.

ajay: thanks all — rolling follow-ups. if anyone finds counterexamples, drop logs here. :thumbsup:
